rv.q: Instead, you admire the production for its sometimes brilliant ideas.
It’s a dazzlingly abstract device to maintain the momentum of an otherwise overly long evening, with quite extraordinary results that feel both fresh and at times grating in equal measure.

Trains – a recurring portent of doom and the eventual cause of Anna’s death – are conjured audibly through chilling collective screeches from the ensemble. And sharing the stage at all times is a trio of live musicians playing Paddy Cunneen’s by turns jaunty and tender compositions.
Overall, I feel it was perhaps too broad of a take on this interesting story, as we lose the drive of our protagonist at times.

cn.t: Dormer shines in a theatrically ambitious adaptation that captures Tolstoy's scope and wit, though the production never fully plumbs the novel's emotional depths.
